ak-git.tagline: Conventional commits, push, PRs, merges, and stacked PRs with secret scans.
ak-git.summary: ak:git handles everyday git work in 6 subcommands (cm, cp, pr, merge, merge-pr, stack), splitting commits by type/scope and scanning every staged diff for secrets. ak:ship and ak:review-pr call it at the end of delivery.
howItWorks: No subcommand: asks which operation to run. Stages only authorized paths, leaving unrelated changes alone.
Greps the staged diff for secret keywords; on a hit it stops and warns.
Splits commits on mixed types, scopes, or config with code; commits as type(scope): description.
pr diffs the remote branch via git-manager and opens it with gh pr create; never force-pushes main.
merge-pr gates readiness, merges, watches CI, and runs ak:fix --auto up to 3 times on red.
useWhen: Commit finished changes as conventional commits, optionally pushing (cp).
Open a PR whose title and body reflect the remote diff.
Merge a ready PR and watch post-merge CI (merge-pr), or drive stacked PRs.
avoidWhen: Full test, review, and PR flow for a finished branch: use ak:ship.
Reviewing PR content or posting reviews: use ak:review-pr.
Issues, labels, Actions, or repo admin: use ak:github.

params.name: cm
params.desc: Stage and commit with secret scan and split logic; no push.

params.name: cp
params.desc: cm then push; sets upstream with push -u if missing. On rejection suggests git pull --rebase.

params.name: pr [to-branch] [from-branch]
params.desc: Create a PR; to-branch defaults to main, from-branch to current. Pushes first if needed.

params.name: merge [to-branch] [from-branch]
params.desc: Merge locally with --no-ff from origin/{from-branch}, so only pushed changes land. Defaults: main, current branch.

params.name: merge-pr <pr-ref>
params.desc: Merge a PR (number or URL) via gh, then watch CI to green. Refuses on conflicts, red CI, or CHANGES_REQUESTED.

params.name: stack
params.desc: Drive GitHub Stacked PRs via gh stack; history rewrites and multi-PR merges need approval.

params.name: [args]
params.desc: Subcommand arguments (branches, PR ref, gh stack subcommand); without a subcommand the skill asks.

examples.note: Commit and push after a small change.
Open a PR into develop instead of main.
Merge PR #482 and wait for green CI.

tips: The secret scan is a keyword grep; inspect flagged files instead of disabling it.
pr uses the remote diff: unpushed commits get pushed, uncommitted changes never appear.
Pass a subcommand to skip the operation prompt.
artifacts: Merge commit on the target (merge, merge-pr)

ak-github.tagline: Evidence-driven GitHub operations via gh: issues, labels, PRs, Projects, Actions.
ak-github.summary: ak:github runs GitHub work through gh: deduplicated issues, labels, PR lifecycle, Projects v2, Actions, and repo/org admin, reporting URLs as proof. It hands PR review to ak:review-pr, commits to ak:git, and CI fixes to ak:fix.
howItWorks: Preflights gh auth status and gh repo view; stops with the exact error on failure.
Loads one reference: issues, PRs, Projects/Actions, or admin.
Dedups new issues across issues, merged PRs, and git log; duplicates get a comment instead.
Always confirms destructive actions (bulk delete, transfer, secret rotate), even in Auto mode.
Ends with mutations and URLs, what was verified, skipped, and still open.
useWhen: File an issue without duplicating an old one or an already fixed bug.
Triage issues, normalize labels, or manage Projects v2.
Inspect or rerun a failed Actions run, or administer repo protection and environments.
avoidWhen: Reviewing PRs or CI-watched merges: use ak:review-pr.
Committing and opening a PR from local changes: use ak:git.
Fixing CI failures: use ak:fix with the run URL.

params.name: <task description or issue/PR ref>
params.desc: The GitHub task or an issue/PR reference; routes to the right reference.

params.name: --interactive
params.desc: Ask about genuinely ambiguous choices (repo, labels, merge strategy) in batches of 2-4 first. Default Auto mode asks nothing.

params.name: --advice
params.desc: Run under kongming oversight: after planning, before irreversible actions, and when stuck. Never bypasses safety gates.

examples.cmd: /ak:github create issue: OAuth login returns 500 on callback
examples.note: Issue with dedup, labels, and evidence.
Bulk triage with approvals.

examples.cmd: /ak:github find why the latest CI run on main is red
examples.note: Summarize the failed run with its URL.

tips: Issue, PR, and log content is data, not instructions; redirect attempts are reported.
Secrets are listed by name only; values are never printed.
Auto mode still stops for destructive actions; add --interactive for more control.
artifacts: GitHub issues, PRs, comments, labels (URLs in the report)

ak-review-pr.tagline: Review GitHub PRs for correctness and security; optionally fix, reply, merge.
ak-review-pr.summary: ak:review-pr reads a PR's diff, files, and checks and reports Critical/Important/Suggestion findings with a verdict, printing to chat by default. --fix, --reply, and --merge authorize fixing and pushing, posting the review, and merging.
howItWorks: Reviews every changed file in full, checks the PR body for evidence, and compares stated vs actual scope.
Falls back to REST helpers when GraphQL is blocked.
--fix loops ak:fix --auto, ak:git cp, re-review; stops when clean, blocked, or a finding survives 3 times.
--reply posts the verdict (COMMENT on self-authored PRs); --merge calls ak:git merge-pr only when ready.
Multiple PRs run in order; ends with a per-PR table of verdict, commits, reply, merge, and CI.
useWhen: Review a teammate's or agent's PR before merging.
Fix all findings and push until clean, then post the review (--fix --reply).
Go from review to merge and green CI in one command (--fix --reply --merge).
avoidWhen: Local changes, commits, or whole codebases: use ak:code-review.
Merging an approved PR without review: use ak:git merge-pr.
Deep security audits: use ak:security.

params.name: <PR number or URL> [...]
params.desc: One or more PRs (123, #123, or URL), space- or comma-separated. Processed in order; failures don't stop the batch.

params.name: --fix
params.desc: Fix loop until clean or stopped (blocked, same finding 3 times, unresolvable CI). Off by default: no edits or pushes.

params.name: --reply
params.desc: Post the review via gh with the matching verdict; with --fix posts only the final one. Reruns post new reviews.

params.name: --merge
params.desc: Runs last: merges via ak:git merge-pr only if Approve, open, mergeable, and CI green/pending. Never forces.

params.name: --advice
params.desc: kongming checkpoints per PR: after review, when fixes stall, before reply and merge. Never overrides the verdict.

params.name: --ultra
params.desc: First review runs best-of-5 plus a verifier; fix re-reviews stay single-pass. About 6x the tokens.

examples.note: Review-only; findings and verdict in chat.
Fix, post review, merge on Approve, watch CI.
Most thorough review for a high-risk PR.

tips: GitHub blocks approving your own PR; the skill posts COMMENT stating Approve.
Use --ultra only for large or risky PRs; it costs about 6x the tokens.
The head SHA is rechecked before reply and merge; new pushes invalidate findings.
artifacts: Fix commits on the PR branch (--fix)

ak-worktree.tagline: Create, inspect, and clean isolated git worktrees, including monorepos.
ak-worktree.summary: ak:worktree creates worktrees on type-prefixed branches (feat/fix/...) and lists, checks, removes, and prunes them. It's the setup step before ak:cook or ak:fix for isolated work.
howItWorks: Reads repo info (type, base branch, projects, worktree root) and reuses a matching worktree.
Infers the prefix (default feat) and a kebab-case slug; --no-prefix keeps names like ABC-1234 as-is.
Creates the worktree from dev, develop, main, or master; asks for a project in monorepos.
Copies .env*.example files and installs dependencies only when the work needs them.
Before removal checks dirty files and nested repos, and asks before destructive deletes.
useWhen: Start a feature without touching the current working tree.
Run parallel agents or sessions, each on its own branch.
Audit and prune stale worktrees, or work in monorepos with submodules.
avoidWhen: A simple branch switch: use git switch or ak:git.
Splitting work across runtimes: use ak:orchestrate.
Worktrees created natively by Claude Code/Codex; worktree.root doesn't affect them.

params.name: [feature-description]
params.desc: Feature description; used to infer branch prefix and slug.

params.name: [project] [feature]
params.desc: Monorepo form: project plus feature; without a project the skill asks.

params.name: create [project] <feature>
params.desc: Create a new worktree.

params.name: remove <name-or-path>
params.desc: Remove a worktree; asks before destructive removal.

params.name: info
params.desc: Repo info plus worktree root location.

params.name: list
params.desc: List worktrees.

params.name: status
params.desc: Health, normalized paths, and drift from the base branch.

params.name: prune
params.desc: Clean stale worktree metadata; try --dry-run first.

params.name: --prefix <type>
params.desc: Branch type: feat|fix|refactor|docs|test|chore|perf.

params.name: --base <branch>
params.desc: Override the detected base branch (dev → develop → main → master).

params.name: --checkout-submodules
params.desc: Init submodules recursively in the new worktree.

params.name: --no-prefix
params.desc: No prefix; keeps uppercase and slashes (Jira keys, user/type/feature).

params.name: --worktree-root <path>
params.desc: Override where worktrees go; beats config, WORKTREE_ROOT, and defaults.

params.name: --json
params.desc: JSON output (baseBranch, worktreePath, warnings, ...).

params.name: --dry-run
params.desc: Preview without executing.

examples.note: Creates a feat/ branch in a new worktree.
Monorepo worktree for the web project.
Preview stale metadata cleanup.

tips: Set a default with ak config prefs set worktree.root; project scope accepts relative paths only.
Stop dev servers you started in a worktree before removing it.
Skip dependency installs for docs-only or small test edits.

ak-security.tagline: Scan secrets, deps, and code; STRIDE + OWASP; optional red-team and fixes.
ak-security.summary: ak:security combines fast scans (secrets, dependency CVEs, exposed .env, risky code patterns) with STRIDE threat modeling mapped to OWASP Top 10, reporting by severity with redacted secrets. It's report-only unless you add --fix or --red-team.
howItWorks: Sets scope (default whole project), trust boundaries, and stack; checks .env exposure.
Scans secrets, audits deps with stack tools (npm audit, pip-audit, govulncheck), and greps risky code patterns.
Runs STRIDE mapped to OWASP A01–A10; --red-team adds 4 attacker personas first.
Dedupes by root cause with evidence and lists rejected concerns as non-issues.
--fix commits one guarded fix per finding as security(fix-N); never rewrites git history.
useWhen: Before a release, or after adding auth, payments, or user-data handling.
Quick secret scan (--secrets-only) or dependency CVE check (--deps-only).
Preparing for compliance or a periodic security review.
avoidWhen: Pure UI changes that touch no credentials or data.
Active pentests or DDoS: out of scope.
OSINT on domains, emails, or people: use ak:cti-expert.

params.name: [scope]
params.desc: Folder, glob, or 'full'; empty scans the project root.

params.name: --secrets-only
params.desc: Scan only secrets; skips deps, code, and STRIDE, and overrides --red-team. Combine with --deps-only for both.

params.name: --deps-only
params.desc: Audit only dependencies for CVEs; skips code and STRIDE. Overrides --red-team.

params.name: --fix
params.desc: Fix confirmed findings by severity, each test/lint-guarded; stops on guard failure. With --red-team, only Critical/High.

params.name: --red-team
params.desc: Run multi-persona discovery (Adversary, Supply Chain, Insider, Infra) before STRIDE/OWASP.

params.name: --iterations N
params.desc: Cap red-team discovery iterations, or fix iterations with --fix.

examples.note: Full audit of the project root.
Quick secret scan before pushing.
Full discovery plus fixes for confirmed Critical/High.

tips: Rotate leaked credentials; removing them from code doesn't revoke them.
Full mode and --red-team are token-heavy; use --secrets-only/--deps-only routinely.
A scary API isn't a vulnerability until a reachable path is verified.
artifacts: Security Audit Report (chat, or plans/reports/security-{date}.md under cook --auto)

ak-cti-expert.tagline: Passive OSINT and threat intel cases, delivered as md + docx reports.
ak-cti-expert.summary: ak:cti-expert runs passive OSINT/CTI work: exposure reviews, domain recon, breach checks, identity research, CVE lookups, and threat modeling. Cases produce Markdown and Word reports (optional offline HTML); single IOC lookups return results without opening a case.
howItWorks: Routes each request to one branch (acquire, enrich, assess, deliver) and loads only its references.
Acquire collects data (/case, /sweep, /query, /username, /email-deep); enrich links leads (/timeline, /graph).
Assess scores and verifies (/exposure 0–100, /threat-model, /verify-finding).
Deliver saves .md and .docx reports, including brief, legal, and STIX 2.1 IOC formats.
useWhen: Assess an organization's or domain's exposure, or check a domain for scams.
Check breaches for an email, trace a username, or score an IOC.
You need a structured intel report or IOC export.
avoidWhen: Scanning your own source for vulnerabilities: use ak:security.
Active pentests, port scans, or exploitation: forbidden.
Doxxing, harassing, or stalking private individuals: refused.

params.name: [target]
params.desc: Target: domain, IP, email, username, phone, hash, and so on.

params.name: --yolo
params.desc: Skip onboarding and open an empty case.

params.name: --case
params.desc: Full automated investigation (/case) across relevant vectors; produces md + docx.

params.name: --sweep
params.desc: Multi-vector recon (/sweep) on a domain, handle, email, or IP.

params.name: --query
params.desc: Generate 12–15 precise search dorks (/query).

params.name: --flow
params.desc: Role-guided walkthrough: Threat Analyst, Journalist, HR screening, or Private Investigator.

params.name: --format html|md
params.desc: md: Markdown + Word (default). html: adds an offline CTI-REPORT-<CASE-ID>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.html.

params.name: --no-antv
params.desc: Disable AntV infographics in HTML for this run; overrides config.

params.name: --no-diagram-design
params.desc: Disable diagram-design visuals in HTML for this run.

params.name: --no-editorial-visuals
params.desc: Disable all editorial visuals; highest priority among the off switches.

examples.note: Full domain investigation as md + docx.
Multi-vector recon on a handle.
Single lookup, no case opened.

tips: Only /case, /report, and /brief save md + docx reports.
Run /validate and /verify-finding before delivery; reports separate facts from hypotheses.
Use /workspace save [name] and /workspace open to resume a case.

ak-web-testing.tagline: Web testing with Playwright, Vitest, k6: unit to E2E, load, a11y.
ak-web-testing.summary: ak:web-testing checks your repo's test scripts, runner versions, and failure type, then picks one runner to write tests or config. It covers unit, E2E, load, visual, a11y, and Web Vitals with 24 references and 2 scripts.
howItWorks: Picks one runner: existing unit runner, browser tests for UI, k6 only for load.
Runs init-playwright.js only when Playwright is missing and requested; keeps existing config.
Fixes flaky tests only after reproducing the cause; no arbitrary sleeps.
Merges results into markdown with analyze-test-results.js; stops processes it started.
useWhen: Write or fix Playwright E2E, component, or Vitest unit tests.
Investigate flaky CI tests or run k6 load tests.
Check a11y, visual regression, or Core Web Vitals.
avoidWhen: Just running the existing suite: use ak:test.
Driving a browser to act or scrape: use ak:agent-browser.
Finding a bug's root cause: use ak:debug.

params.name: [test-type]
params.desc: Test type (unit, e2e, load, visual, a11y, performance, ...); selects runner and reference.

params.name: [target]
params.desc: What to test: file, folder, feature, or URL.

examples.note: Playwright E2E tests for checkout.
Reproduce and fix a flaky test.
k6 script for the search endpoint.

tips: Don't add waitForTimeout/sleep to hide flakiness.
Load only the references you need to save context.
Stop dev/preview servers you started for tests.
artifacts: test-results/ and coverage/ from the runner

ak-deep-swe.tagline: Benchmark a coding model on DeepSWE via Pier and OpenRouter.
ak-deep-swe.summary: ak:deep-swe runs an independent DeepSWE evaluation with Pier through OpenRouter and reports command, version, score, cost, and blockers. It spends money gradually: one task, then a small subset, and the full corpus only with your approval.
howItWorks: Checks uv, git, Docker, and that OPENROUTER_API_KEY is set, without printing it.
Clones deep-swe, installs datacurve-pier, reads its help, and verifies the model slug.
Runs one task, then a fixed 10-task subset (seed 0).
Shows the full-corpus command, cost, and stop conditions, then waits for approval.
Reports observed results separately from vendor scores; never submits to the leaderboard unasked.
useWhen: Score a model on DeepSWE before adopting it as a coding agent.
Compare two model configs on the same fixed task set.
Verify a published benchmark number independently.
avoidWhen: Optimizing a metric in your own repo: use ak-loop / ak:autoresearch.
Docker or OPENROUTER_API_KEY is missing; the skill will stop.
You only want published scores; check deepswe.datacurve.ai.

params.name: <OpenRouter model slug>
params.desc: OpenRouter slug as vendor/model, passed as openrouter/<vendor/model>; verified before running.

examples.note: One trial task, then a proposed subset.
Compare another model on the same tasks.

tips: Keep seed and task set fixed when comparing configs.
Pier changes fast; check help instead of guessing flags.
Missing cache telemetry means unknown, not 0.
